title: The evaluation dashboard: how Claude and the whole system perform, and every model's precision, recall, F1 and accuracy
request: The owner asked for an evaluation part to see the performance of Claude and of the entire system, and a dashboard with every model's evaluation metrics: precision, recall, F1 and accuracy.
spec: dclab_core evaluation (EvaluationBoard v1, score, from_twin_steps, from_ledger), dclab_rnd evaluation (the board from the twin folder and the ledger), GET /api/evaluation, the Admin Evaluation tab.
plan: Score every answerer the same way at every point against its truth, with the cases behind each number.
Set Claude beside the system step by step with the mode the fixed rule recommends.
Check every metric against cases counted by hand.

decisions.decision: One rule for undefined ratios for every kind of answer, as scikit-learn's zero_division=0 where the truth has positives.
decisions.why: Three kinds of answer with three conventions made the same miss read as a dash in one table and a zero in another.

decisions.decision: A person's pick is not scored as accuracy; it stays in the twin matrix as a preference.
decisions.why: The pick makes the chosen side right by construction.

decisions.decision: A person's correction of an answer they were shown is left out of the scores.
decisions.why: It is accepted only where the shown answer was wrong, so it would score that answer wrong every time.

change: dclab_core/evaluation.py (new), contracts, conformance, schemas; dclab_rnd/evaluation.py (new), agentic/pages/evaluation.py (new), pages/__init__.py, accounts/guard.py, web/src/views/admin.html; tests/test_evaluation.py (new).

findings.defect: The gate failed on the new contract.
findings.scenario: The schema baseline and the conformance entry of the board were missing.
findings.cause: The contract was registered without its baseline or its adapter line.
findings.fix: The baseline is written and the board is library output in the conformance tables.

findings.defect: The system arm was counted twice in every twin run.
findings.scenario: A run's steps and its expert record's steps carried the same system answer and truth, so the system had two cases where there was one.
findings.cause: Both files were read and the system was keyed only by its name.
findings.fix: The same system answer to the same question in one session counts once, and the twin matrix reads the run's own steps only.

findings.defect: A person's correction of what they were shown scored the shown answer wrong by construction.
findings.scenario: With every label a correction, the rule showed an accuracy of zero.
findings.cause: Such a label is accepted only when it contradicts the shown answer.
findings.fix: Corrections are left out of the scores and the page says which truths it reads.

findings.defect: Blind labels were scored without their weights.
findings.scenario: The blind draw over-samples disagreements, so every shown answerer looked worse than it is.
findings.cause: The weight of each blind label was ignored.
findings.fix: Counts are weighed by the label's weight and the interval reads the effective number of cases.

findings.defect: A person's pick was scored as accuracy.
findings.scenario: One pick gave the chosen side a perfect score and the other none.
findings.cause: The pick's truth is the chosen answer.
findings.fix: Picks stay in the twin matrix as a preference and are not in the model table.

findings.defect: A set answerer that never answered showed perfect scores.
findings.scenario: Two empty truths and no answers gave a precision and a recall of one.
findings.cause: Nothing to find and nothing claimed was read as perfect even with no answer.
findings.fix: Without an answer the numbers are undefined.

findings.defect: Undefined precision was handled three different ways and the macro left out classes only answered.
findings.scenario: All positives missed showed a dash; a class only predicted did not count in the macro.
findings.cause: Each kind had its own convention.
findings.fix: One convention for all kinds and the macro over every class answered or true.

findings.defect: The macro was computed after the classes were cut to fifty.
findings.scenario: Sixty-one classes gave a macro over the first fifty in alphabetical order.
findings.cause: The stored list's bound was applied before the mean.
findings.fix: The macro is over every class; only the stored list is cut.

findings.defect: A level or a threshold was compared as a string.
findings.scenario: A rule's one against a label's one point zero was scored wrong.
findings.cause: Every non-flag point was a choice.
findings.fix: A level and the numeric points are compared as numbers.

findings.defect: The page counted each scored answer as a case.
findings.scenario: One pick showed two cases with a truth.
findings.cause: The total summed every answerer's count.

findings.defect: Rows could not be filtered by their truth and the twin table had no time.
findings.scenario: Typing planted found nothing; the plan asked for time beside cost.
findings.cause: The filter read only the answerer and the point.
findings.fix: The filter reads the truth too and the table shows each side's time.

findings.defect: A flag answer that was not a flag was read by its truthiness.
findings.scenario: The word no against a true truth counted as a hit.
findings.cause: Any value was cast to a flag.
findings.fix: A value that is not a flag is no answer.

findings.defect: A test expected an undefined F1 where precision and recall were both zero.
findings.cause: The expectation was wrong: F1 is zero then.

outcome: The dashboard shows each model's scores with the cases behind them; the live measurement is open.
lessons: A truth chosen by a person between two answers is a preference, not a score.
Write the convention for undefined ratios once and apply it to every kind.
risks: Few labelled cases yet: most rows will read undecided or carry wide intervals.
